title: Build a form validator in TypeScript — 3 turns
description: Three turns build a form validator: turn 1 required field check, turn 2 format validation (email, number), turn 3 async validation.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `required()` and `validate()` in `src/validator.ts`. required: return valid=true if value.trim() is non-empty, else return the error message. validate: loop through validators, call each with value, return first failing result, or {valid: true} if all pass. Run `npm test -- --forceExit`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `email()`, `isNumber()`, and `minLength()`. email: use a regex like `/^[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+$/` to check format. isNumber: use `!isNaN(Number(value))` but reject empty string. minLength: check `value.length >= min`. Run `npm test -- --forceExit` and fix any failures.

Final step: implement `validateAsync()` — loop through validators, await each one (whether sync or async), return first failure or {valid: true}. Run `npm test -- --forceExit` — all 11 tests must pass.
success_criteria: isNumber accepts numeric strings, rejects non-numeric
validate returns first error from chain
validateAsync handles both sync and async validators
